messages:
alexa: FYI support reported more onboarding friction: sample that imports 'redwood' in a Next.js edge function loses types & runtime behavior depending on bundler. repro attached.

ryan: can you paste the exact import pattern? ESM default import vs named?

alexa: simple: `import Redwood from 'redwood'` in pages/api/edge.ts. Next's esbuild-based bundler inlines the package and picks the esm build, which is fine runtime but tsserver still points at dist/cjs/index.d.ts in some editors.

ezra: sounds like our published package has types only under dist/cjs and dist/esm, but no top-level types field. TS falls back to package level resolution quirks.

sasha: also a bundler quirk: when Next bundles for edge, it does a resolve->browser field-ish rewrite and sometimes rewrites conditional exports. So two problems: editor type path and bundle behavior diverge.

alexa: example error: "Could not find a declaration file for module 'redwood'." Users delete node_modules/.cache and occasionally that fixes it; but that's not a DX story.

ryan: short-term patch: add "types": "dist/types/index.d.ts" at package root so editors have deterministic path. Longer: use exports.types mapping per subpath so TS knows which file for './edge' and './browser'.

ezra: proposal: exports map like:
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs",
    "types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts"
  },
  "./edge": {
    "import": "./dist/edge/index.mjs",
    "types": "./dist/edge/index.d.ts"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
"types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts"
```
This covers editors and offers an explicit edge subpath.

sasha: agree but caveat: some bundlers don't honor exports.types in older TS. Having the top-level "types" field is the easiest win.

alexa: unrelated but related: our retry/auth adapter is currently a side-effect in cjs bundle only. When esbuild tree-shakes it away in some client bundles, the wrapper is not applied -> requests have no automatic retries in browser-edge builds.

ryan: we need deterministic side-effects. Either make adapter a tiny explicit import in the README samples (`import 'redwood/adapter'`) or keep it as explicit top-level import in the main entrypoint so bundlers can't tree-shake it when users import the SDK.

ezra: prefer explicit tiny module 'redwood/adapter' which documents it's a side-effecting module. That avoids surprising application-level globals. We can then make the main entrypoints import it, but also docs ask user to import it when they need the global shim.

sasha: for packaging, we should ensure the adapter exists in dist/adapter.{mjs,cjs} and exports a no-op for environments that don't support fetch. Keep it tiny ~40 lines.

ci-bot: ci/samples-edge-run  
  sample-edge-tests: 1 failed, 12 passed. See artifacts.

alexa: timeline: i can push a sample PR today to add top-level "types" and update Next edge example to import 'redwood/edge' explicitly. Then we open a follow-up to add adapter module and exports.types mapping.

ryan: please also add a tiny test in our sample suite that runs TS typecheck against the sample with `tsc --noEmit` to catch this in CI.

ezra: agree. i'll draft the package-change PR: top-level types + adapter + dist/edge build + docs. I'll add a changelog note about pinning if people rely on require semantics.

alexa: thanks. tagging @sasha to own the tiny adapter implementation. :+1:

sasha: on it, will push WIP later today.

ryan: one more thought: update our publish CI to validate `npm pack` consumer resolution with node, webpack, and esbuild to avoid regressions. low effort, high payoff.

alexa: love that. adding a ticket.

ci-bot: ticket created: INF-1234 "validate package resolution in node/webpack/esbuild"

alexa: closing loop here. will merge sample patch after green CI. thanks team.
